title: Sunrise inference scrapbook - morning triage
content:
Quick morning dump - trying to capture things before I forget.

Date: 2024-08-22 (sunrise shift)
Mood: slightly caffeinated, worried about tail latencies on A100 pool.

Snapshot / what woke me up:
- Last night prod p99 spiked twice for text-gen routes (hosted-api/model-xlarge) around 02:10 and 03:44 UTC.
- Both spikes correlated with long KV cache misses + microbatch pressure when seq_len > 1536.
- Canary on dedicated GPUs (A100-80) didn't show the same magnitude; suspect routing fallback to smaller-hosted instances + quantized model causing jitter.

Immediate triage TODOs (high priority)
1) Reproduce locally: run small replay of the two suspect requests from logs. Command: ./tools/replay_requests --start 2024-08-22T02:08:00Z --end 2024-08-22T02:12:00Z --route text-gen/model-xlarge --limit 500.
   - Expected: see p99 ~300ms baseline, observed: 2.1s.
   - Quick check: curl tracing headers to see which variant handled the request.
2) Inspect KV cache eviction around those timestamps. Look at per-shard eviction counters: /metrics?name=kv_cache_evictions&since=2024-08-22T01:00Z. Hypothesis: hot prefixes evicted due to burst causing thrash.
3) Rollback candidate: temp increase cache size on hosted tier by +20% (config key: runtime.cache.kv.max_entries). Test on canary first.

Notes / clues to keep in mind
- There is an open PR that touched the batch scheduler heuristics (PR #842). It changed the headroom calculation from 0.15->0.1 for microbatch merging. Could reduce batching headroom and increase opportunistic merging causing KV misses.
- Recent infra update: libtorch 2.2 build on dedicated but hosted still on 2.1. Differences in allocator behavior might explain variance.

Perf numbers (yesterday baseline - aggregated)
- p50: 72ms
- p95: 210ms
- p99: 1.98s (two spikes pushed this up)
- avg tokens/sec per GPU (A100 pool): 420

Hypotheses (ordered):
A) Batching headroom reduction -> more aggressive merging -> longer per-request KV lookups -> higher p99 when sequence lengths vary.
B) Cache eviction/rehydration thrash for prefixes around 1024-1536 due to recent model rollout toggles.
C) Torch allocator fallback on some hosted nodes -> temporary stall when allocating large KV cache pages.

Experiments to run today
- EXP-1 (fast): Locally run replay with headroom param set to 0.15 (old value). Command: ./tools/replay_requests --headroom 0.15 --variant canary. Measure p99.
- EXP-2 (medium): Increase runtime.cache.kv.max_entries by 20% in a canary pool and run synthetic workload of long seqs. Monitor evictions.
- EXP-3 (slow): Launch canary with libtorch 2.2 on hosted infra (if infra consent) to compare allocator metrics.

Quick reproduction checklist (for oncall or next engineer)
- Pull latest logs: ./scripts/fetch_logs --service runtime --from 2024-08-22T01:45Z --to 2024-08-22T03:00Z --out /tmp/triage-logs
- Run replay against local runtime with same config the router used (check router trace in logs).
- Confirm which model-variant served the requests (quantized vs full fp16).
- Check GPU memory pressure graphs (prometheus: node_gpu_memory_used_bytes).

Commands & snippets I used / will use
- replay: ./tools/replay_requests --ticket RWI-1293 --rate 200/s --duration 120 --out /tmp/replay.json
- fetch traces: ./tools/get_traces --trace-id 20240822-0210-hosted-xyz --format json | jq .
- quick perf: python tools/quick_latency_summary.py /tmp/replay.json

Notes to self (things to log in the final postmortem)
- Timestamp ranges of spikes + router decisions.
- PRs + deploys around the timeframe (PR #842 likely suspect).
- Exact config differences between canary and hosted (libtorch version, cache size, headroom).
- Whether any autoscaler-induced node churn happened (check cluster-autoscaler logs).

Low-priority / backlog items (may triage to next sprint)
- Add finer-grained KV-cache metrics: per-prefix hit-rate in top 100 prefixes. (ticket idea: RWI-1377)
- Investigate bloom-filter tuning for prefix membership test to reduce unnecessary KV lookups.
- Add a small synthetic test that fills prefix cache and then issues long tail accesses to reproduce thrash deterministically.

Calendar / schedule for today
- 09:00-09:30 standup + quick sync with Leo (triage handoff)
- 09:30-11:00 repro + EXP-1 run
- 11:00-12:00 canary config change (EXP-2) and monitoring window
- 13:00-14:00 write short incident summary if we confirm root cause

People to ping if stuck
- @Leo Martinez - routing heuristics owner
- @Hannah Kim - batch scheduler author
- @Diego - infra allocator questions (cc infra channel)

Open questions (to answer before finaling incident)
- Why did dedicated A100 not experience the same spike? (allocator / build diff?)
- Did the router prefer smaller-hosted variants due to capacity fallback? Need routing logs.
- Any correlation with maintenance events around 02:00-03:00 UTC?

Random micro-notes (brain dump)
- Consider quick safeguard: temporary automated fallback to older batch heuristic if p99 > 1.2s for 5m. Could be a circuit-breaker.
- If we move cache size, monitor cost impact for hosted tier — get cost estimate from finance.

End-of-shift handoff snippet (copy to slack):
- TL;DR: p99 spikes at 02:10 & 03:44 likely from aggressive microbatch headroom change (PR #842) + KV cache thrash on long seqs. Repro plan running. Canaries: EXP-2 underway to increase KV entries. Will post update by 12:30 UTC.

-- Nina
